Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the VAT ID. Quick answers and options below. I’m copying Marissa (Finance) and Monica (CS ops) so we all have the same record.

1) Collection accounts (preferred rails)
- EUR (SEPA): If you can send a SEPA transfer from an EU bank, use:
  Bank: ING Bank (NL)
  Account name: Redwood Inference B.V.
  IBAN: NL91INGB0000001234
  BIC/SWIFT: INGBNL2A
  (SEPA transfers typically avoid correspondent fees and are cheapest/fastest across the EU.)

- USD (SWIFT): If payer must send USD, use our USD correspondent details in the attached wire PDF. Note: USD SWIFT payments will often traverse correspondent banks and may incur intermediary deductions.

2) Intermediary/correspondent bank fees
- There are three common fee options to request from your bank: OUR (sender pays all fees), BEN (beneficiary pays all fees), SHA (sender/beneficiary split).
- Our preference: OUR or SHA (with OUR preferred for large cross-border USD wires). If your bank uses BEN (deducts fees from the transferred amount), Redwood will receive a lower net and we may invoice for the shortfall.
- If you instruct OUR, please confirm with your bank that their system will cover correspondent bank fees — some EU banks default to SHA and won't allow OUR without manual handling.

3) VAT handling
- We have an EU entity registered for VAT. If Novum is a business and provides a valid VAT ID (the HU number you gave looks good), we can issue the invoice without Dutch VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism. Please include your VAT ID on the payment remittance or in the payment reference so our billing system can clear it.

I've attached a short PDF with the formal wire instructions for both EUR and USD and the expected remittance reference format. Could you please confirm which account and payment option your bank will use (SEPA/EUR vs SWIFT/USD and OUR/SHA/BEN)? If they will do BEN, we’ll flag finance to expect a shortfall and coordinate the follow-up.

Best,
Rishi

Subject: Re: Payment collection: collection account currency, correspondent bank chain, and fee handling

Hi Elena — Marissa from Finance here. Two quick operational points to avoid surprises:

- Policy on correspondent deductions: Redwood Finance policy is that the invoiced gross amount must be received. We do not absorb intermediary/correspondent bank fees as a standard. If your bank deducts fees (BEN), we will either request the payer to top up the shortfall or issue a shortfall invoice that references the original invoice number.

- Preferred instruction: Please instruct your bank to use OUR for the full chain where possible. If your bank refuses OUR, SHA is acceptable but please confirm the expected net amount so we can reconcile.

- If you are paying by SEPA/EUR to the IBAN Rishi shared, intermediary fees are unlikely. For any SWIFT/USD routing where correspondents are involved, please ask your treasury to provide the cover chain or correspondent bank nodes so we can check with our bank to match remittance exactly. Listings should include intermediate BICs and intermediary account numbers.

- Treasury contact: treasury@redwood.inference.com (for bank-level matching)

Thanks — once you confirm the rail (SEPA vs SWIFT) and fee option (OUR vs SHA/BEN), we’ll mark the invoice as “ready to match” on our side and avoid a reconciliation lag.

Kind regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
